title: Protocol to visualize glycan-mediated binding between virus and human blood mononuclear cells using thin-section transmission electron microscopy
protocol: Place 10–15 mL of cell suspension into a 15 mL tube.
Stand the tube in the incubator and allow cells to settle by gravity.
Carefully remove the media and unsettled cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet very gently with 5 mL prewarmed DPBS and allow to settle by gravity.
Carefully remove the DPBS and unsettled cells and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL prewarmed DPBS.
Transfer the cells to a 1.5 mL conical screw cap tube.
Place at 37°C until needed, allowing the cells to settle during this period.
Prepare the virus or VLPs for the assay while the cells are settling.
Treat with 450 U PNGase F enzyme in glycobuffer 2 in a total reaction volume of 10 μL.
Incubate the PNGase F treated samples at 37°C for 1 hour.
Set up an equivalent reaction in glycobuffer 2 without adding enzyme as an untreated control.
Cut Thermanox supports into rectangle shapes with the top right-hand corner clipped.
Position the cut corner in the top right position for orientation.
Submerge clean scissors into 100% ethanol and allow to air dry before use.
Use clean scissors to score a circle shape into the surface of each support.
Clean Thermanox supports by submerging them into 100% ethanol and allowing them to air dry.
Place clean and dry supports onto filter paper inside a petri dish, scored side up.
Pipette a 5–10 μL droplet of poly-L-lysine (1 mg/mL) into each scored circle.
Allow the poly-L-lysine droplets to sit for 30 minutes.
Monitor the droplets to ensure they do not evaporate too quickly.
Wick off excess poly-L-lysine using lint-free tissues.
Allow supports to air dry at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 20–30 minutes.
Store Thermanox supports in a closed disposable petri dish at 4°C, with the poly-L-lysine side up, up to 24 hours before use.
Incubate tubes containing cells and virus or VLPs at 4°C for at least 10–15 minutes prior to combining them.
Place all tubes on ice after mixing to maintain entry non-permissive temperatures.
Prepare a 24-well tissue culture plate by pipetting approximately 1.5 mL of 2.5% glutaraldehyde in PBS into the appropriate number of wells.
Carefully remove most of the DPBS from above the settled cells, leaving about 100 μL.
Gently pipette to resuspend the cell pellet.
Transfer 10 μL of cell suspension to chilled virus or VLP tubes.
Mix cells and virus/VLP by gently pipetting the mixture five times.
Immediately transfer approximately 3–5 μL of the mixture to the poly-L-lysine coated region on a Thermanox support.
Allow the sample to bind to the poly-L-lysine for 5–10 minutes, ensuring droplets do not dry due to evaporation.
Gently invert Thermanox supports onto the 2.5% glutaraldehyde in PBS.
Place each Thermanox support in its own well on the 24-well plate.
Store samples at 4°C until processing for EM.
Remove Thermanox supports from the glutaradehyde solution and place them sample side up in a 12-well culture dish.
Wash the supports in PBS twice for 40 s each at 150 W without vacuum.
Post-fix the Thermanox supports in 1% osmium tetroxide for 12 min (2 min power on, 2 min power off, repeated) at 80 W under vacuum.
Dehydrate samples through an ethanol series (30%, 50%, 70%, 90%, and 100%) for 40 s each at 150 W without vacuum.
Repeat the final 100% ethanol step.
Infiltrate the sample with LX112 resin in a 50% ethanol: 50% resin mixture for 3 min at 250 W under vacuum.
Fill BEEM capsules (size 3) with resin and invert over marked sample area.
Snap the BEEM capsules off the dish using pliers once polymerized.
Remove the BEEM capsules from the resin block prior to sectioning the samples.
Trim the resin block to the region of the sample as marked by the scored imprint.
Section the blocks at 60–70 nm using an ultramicrotome with a diamond knife.
Collect the sections onto specimen grids.
Post stain the grids with 5% uranyl acetate in 50% ethanol for 90 s.
Rinse the grids three times in pure water, wicking excess water away using filter paper.
Stain the grids with Reynold’s lead citrate for 45 s.
Wash the stained grids three times with pure water, wicking excess water away using filter paper.
Allow the grids to air dry and then store them in a grid box until imaging.
Image the grids using a TEM operated at 80 kV.
